get.description:
Rank: exact ticker, then ticker prefix, then name substring.

Each band is alphabetical within itself. A blank query returns no results rather
than the whole table.

The scan's buy-to-own list, rendered exactly as it was scored.

Reads ``BuyCandidateRow`` through the **read-only** trading session (§4.3 — the API
writes nothing). The web layer does no re-scoring: every field is what the
orchestrator's scan-time scoring produced, so the site and the Telegram card
can never disagree about what the system thinks. An empty table returns an empty
list with a 200, not a 404 — no scan has run yet is a legitimate state.

Sector cards: aggregate daily change, best/worst mover, count, and average IV rank.

Membership comes from ``universe.yaml``'s ``sectors`` map (every universe symbol tagged
with its sector). ``change_pct`` is the warm-tier quote's daily change from the research
DB; a sector with no priced members reports ``change_pct`` as ``None``, never ``0``.
``avg_iv_rank`` averages only members that actually have IV history in the trading DB
(read-only), and the card carries the contributing count so a one-name average is visible.

Cards are returned ordered by ``avg_iv_rank`` descending (premium richness is the
reason to look); sectors with no IV history sort last, preserving their file order.

Daily OHLCV with server-side SMA 50 and 200, in lightweight-charts' field names.

``time`` is ``YYYY-MM-DD`` (lightweight-charts' accepted daily format). SMA 50 and 200
are computed from ``daily_bars`` here so the chart and the technical panel can never
disagree. A symbol with no bars returns empty lists, not an error.

On-demand options-income lens — honest about what it does and doesn't know.

A universe symbol gets real `iv_rank`/`vrp_points` from the trading DB, read-only
(§4.3). An off-universe symbol gets the same shape with `UNKNOWN` and
`coverage.iv_history` false rather than a percentile invented from a short series.
`coverage.option_chain` is always false in P1 — the API holds no IBKR connection, so
`atm_open_interest`/`atm_spread_pct` stay `UNKNOWN` too. Leverage warnings (Task 5.4)
are included for leveraged names via the shared `warnings_for` catalogue.

The newest headlines for one symbol, newest first, each VADER-scored.

The light read behind the position page's news section: it calls the headline loader only,
never `materialize()` (which can start an SEC fundamentals ingest). An unreachable news
source is an empty list, never an error, and nothing is stored. Enrichment tier: headlines
reach the page and never the engine.

Full analysis for one symbol.

404 only when the symbol is not a known filer. Everything else degrades per section.

Return a cached summary if one exists. **Makes no model call and no
``materialize``/fetch.**

A cold-tier search on an obscure ticker must not silently trigger a model call
(design §7), and the same principle applies to the SEC/enrichment fetches
``materialize`` would run. The GET first consults the cache directly; only on a
miss does it build the ``AnalysisResponse`` to compute a stable ``data_as_of`` for
the ``unavailable`` reason, and even then it makes no model call — the client
renders a Generate action rather than a spinner.

post.description:
Generate and cache a summary on demand. Fail-soft: a failed generation returns
``pending`` with a reason, not an error, so the rest of the page is untouched.

get.description:
List approvals, pending by default. ``status=all`` returns decided ones too.

An unknown status value is rejected with 422 (not a silent empty list) — an
operator typo should surface, not look like "no approvals." ``since``/``until``
filter by UTC calendar date, inclusive on both ends.

parameters.name: status

schema.description: Filter by approval status, or `all` for every status (newest first).
schema.title: Status

parameters.description: Filter by approval status, or `all` for every status (newest first).

parameters.name: symbol

schema.description: Filter to one underlying (case-insensitive), matched via the joined CandidateRow. An approval whose candidate has since been pruned (14-day purge) will not match even if its own snapshot still carries the symbol.
schema.title: Symbol

parameters.description: Filter to one underlying (case-insensitive), matched via the joined CandidateRow. An approval whose candidate has since been pruned (14-day purge) will not match even if its own snapshot still carries the symbol.

get.description: One approval in full. 404 if unknown. Joined enrichment degrades to null.

Past full-scan run ids, newest first — lets the Assessed tab browse history.

Registered ahead of ``/assessed`` in this file only for reading order; the two
paths never collide (this one carries no path parameter). Excludes single-ticker
runs (``scan-``/``ticker-`` prefixes) the same way ``_latest_run_id`` does — a
``/scan NVDA`` or a promote attempt is not "a run" in the sense this list means.
The assessed browser: every contract the scan priced, grouped by symbol.

parameters.name: stage

schema.description: Filter to one assessment stage. Unknown values return 422.
schema.title: Stage

parameters.description: Filter to one assessment stage. Unknown values return 422.

get.description:
Working orders by default. ``state=all`` returns everything.

An unknown state value is rejected with 422 (not a silent empty list). Each order carries
the sizing actions linked to it (``sizing``), so an auditor can see why 1 contract went out
when the scan said 3.

parameters.name: days

schema.description: Only orders created in the last N days.
schema.title: Days

parameters.description: Only orders created in the last N days.

get.description:
Recent fills within the last ``days`` days, each naming its contract (from the order's
frozen snapshot, then its candidate; unknown stays null).

Open short option positions from the most recent position snapshot.

``as_of`` is the snapshot's capture time, not request time — the same discipline
P0/P1 M4 fixed for quotes. Long options and stock are excluded. ``delta`` carries
its source through ``Sourced`` so a BS delta never looks identical to an IBKR one.
A position with no snapshot data returns ``null`` for ``mark`` and
``unrealized_pnl``, never ``0.0``.
Autonomy rung, halt state, mode, and command-drain health.

Account values as `Sourced` + the exposure the operator needs before deciding.

The `none` rung is a 200, not a 404: there is no error, there is simply nothing
captured yet, and the client needs a well-formed response saying so in words.

The wheel threads — one thread per symbol, legs in order.

`as_of` is request time here, NOT a snapshot time: campaigns are written on
fill, not captured, so there is no capture time to read. Do not "fix" this to
match the other portfolio routes. Financials are gross of commissions (M0
Task 0.4's pinned semantics — see `src/storage/campaigns.py::_rollup`'s and
`CampaignRow`'s docstrings); `src/reporting/` nets commissions on the same
trades, so a campaign's `net_premium` and the net P&L of its legs differ by
exactly the commission total. A leg whose `CandidateRow` was pruned still
renders with `known: false` — the financials are rolled up from `FillRow` and
survive pruning, so the leg count must not silently disagree with them.

`limit` (default 50, max 200) caps the read because campaigns are never
pruned — the table grows forever, and a response that materialises every row
ever written is an unbounded JSON payload, not a "latest threads" list.

Option expiries grouped by date over a horizon, with what expiry would mean.

The `consequence` mapping, exactly as specified: an ITM short put is
`assigned`; an ITM short call is `called_away` only when the stock is held to
deliver — a naked short call assignment is a short stock position, not a
call-away; any short OTM/ATM is `expires_worthless`; a long option is
`expires_worthless` only when OTM; unknown moneyness is `unknown`, never a
default to `expires_worthless`.

Every position, grouped by underlying — the unit the operator thinks in.

Both cost bases are reported, never one substituted for the other: `avg_cost`
is what IBKR says, `adjusted_cost_basis` is what the collected premium makes
it. The empty rung returns `groups: []` with `source="none"` — an empty list
plus `source="monitor"` would be a claim that the account holds nothing.

One position's page: where it stands now, and the trade that opened it.

The slug is what a Positions row links with: ``2026-11-21_P180`` (an option contract),
``shares``, or ``spread-<id>``. The live figures come from the same snapshot reading
``GET /portfolio/positions`` renders (so the two never disagree); the initial trade comes from
the system's own fills through the builders Home's "Done today" uses. A contract that is no
longer held but was traded by the system still answers, with ``closed`` saying how it ended.
404 when neither the snapshot nor the fills know it. Read-only; never reaches IBKR.

Account value over `range` for the Home hero. Computes nothing itself: a thin render
of `account_value_series`. No history is a 200 with no points, never zeros.

Leg rows grouped under their campaign threads — OVERVIEW's "Excel-shaped
ledger of every position opened and closed", readable in a browser.

The grouping is what stops an assignment reading as a leg that ended for
no reason: a campaign-less leg lands in a synthetic per-symbol thread (M4
Task 4.4), so `n_legs` always equals the sum of every campaign's leg count.

The totals and breakdowns, computed from the same `PnlLeg` list the
ledger renders — a total can never disagree with the rows above it.

`build_summary` raises `ValueError` on a mixed paper/live list (M4 Task
4.5); this route turns that into a `422` naming `mixed_book`, so the
operator picks a book instead of reading a wrong number. A single-book
summary over an empty list is a valid empty summary, not an error.

parameters.name: book

schema.description: Which fills to total. 'all' is refused with 422 mixed_book when both paper and live fills are present, because a total across both is not a number that means anything.
schema.title: Book

parameters.description: Which fills to total. 'all' is refused with 422 mixed_book when both paper and live fills are present, because a total across both is not a number that means anything.

get.description:
The equity curve — one point per journal day, plus the trading days
between them that have no point, so the chart can render a gap rather than
a fabricated straight line.

The route computes nothing: `build_legs` feeds `equity_curve` exactly as it
feeds the ledger. `book=all` is fine *here*, deliberately unlike
`/pnl/summary`: the curve's `cumulative_realized` sums `net_pnl` per point,
and mixing books in a curve is a display choice the client makes, not a
headline total. Do not "fix" one to match the other.

The same rows `/pnl/ledger` returns, under the same filters, as CSV.

Built from the same `build_legs` call the JSON route uses — a second query
would let the two drift. There is no mixed-book refusal here because a CSV
has no headline total to be wrong; the `book` column identifies each row
after export.

The score-vs-outcome evidence's human reader (P3-P4 M6 Task 6.1).

Reads behind the fence CLAUDE.md draws around `src/claude/eval/`: this is the one route in
the phase where that is the intended use, not a breach — `score_outcome_report`'s own notes
already say the weights must be re-derived by hand, and this route only renders them. It
calls `score_outcome_report` and returns exactly what it gets: no bucket recomputed, no
correlation re-derived, no note filtered. `verdict_ledger` and the human-edited scoring
config are read-only from here — `tests/test_web_fence.py` (Task 6.3) asserts no module
under `src/api/` can write either or even name the scoring config by filename.

What the regime limits, the scale-in ladder, the leveraged-ETF ceiling, the floor lots and
Claude's size cut held back, and what that would have earned (web overhaul Part 3, Task 1).

Reads behind the `src/claude/eval/` fence, like `/pnl/system`: this is the human reader
`CLAUDE.md` says everything `eval/` produces is for. It calls `summarize` and returns what it
gets, grouped and ordered; no figure is recomputed here, and nothing on the route can change a
limit, a size or a weight. `since` is the first action day counted (default: every action on
record). Rows not yet valued count and are not valued.

The monthly income target as set, for the More page's control. `source` says whether it
is the web setting, the legacy `web.monthly_income_target_pct`, or nothing.

The month's pay stub. `book` defaults to the running mode: a pay figure across paper
and live is not a number that means anything (same rule as /pnl/summary). Spreads count
only positions whose mode equals the book; shadow and baseline are simulations.

What was opened, closed or rolled on one New York day, as the cards Home shows.

`date` defaults to today in New York. Every card comes from the same `PnlLeg` list (and the
book's spread rows) the pay stub and the calendar read; a roll is one card, paired on its
combo order. The reasons are worked out from stored facts, never generated. `book` defaults
to the running mode, as `/pnl/month` does.

A month of daily realised P&L: each day's net result, after commissions, of what closed
that day (options legs and the book's credit spreads). Days nothing closed are absent.
The day's sizing record: puts the regime, the ladder or Claude's cut trimmed or held back.

One New York day of the spreads picker: each menu Claude was shown, its choice, what was
sent, and every spread any book opened that day. `day` defaults to today in New York.

post.description:
Enqueue a `universe_add` intent. Always `201` — universe_add/universe_remove have no
dedupe key (M7 final-review Fix 1: they are idempotent upserts, so a repeat is always a
fresh command, never a `200` reusing a stale one). `404` for an unknown symbol; `422`
for a non-overridable list.

delete.description:
Enqueue a `universe_remove` intent. Always `201` (see `add_to_universe` — no dedupe
key). `409` if removing an `actively_wheeling` symbol from `would_own` — you cannot stop
being willing to own something you are actively wheeling. `404` for an unknown symbol;
`422` for a non-overridable list.

get.description: Return this user's watchlist items. A second user's items are not returned.

post.description:
Add *symbol* to this user's watchlist. Idempotent: a repeat is 200, not an error.

Returns 201 on first add, 200 on a repeat. 404 if the symbol is not a known filer — we
never create a row that can never resolve to a name. Adding a symbol promotes it to the
warm tier immediately (``warm_symbols`` reads ``WatchlistItemRow``).

delete.description: Remove *symbol* from this user's watchlist. Idempotent: a repeat delete is 204.

post.description: Enqueue an intent. 201 if new, 200 if a dedupe returned the existing row.

get.description: Read one command's status through the read-only engine.

post.description:
Supply the confirm token for a live-mode order-reaching intent.

In paper mode no token was issued, so this is a no-op 204. A command not
awaiting confirmation (already applied, expired, or not an order-reaching
kind) returns 409 — the request does not make sense for that command. A
wrong or missing token is **403**: the caller has not proven authority to
release this order, and the token is NOT cleared, so the command stays
pending (the fail-closed property, M3 Task 3.5).

AccountValueSeries.title: AccountValueSeries
AccountValueSeries.description:
Account value (net liquidation) over a range, for the Home hero chart.

1d/1w plot the intraday portfolio snapshots inside the window (retention:
`storage.portfolio_snapshot_retention_days`); 1m/3m/ytd/all plot one point per EOD journal
close, at that day's 16:00 ET. `latest` is the newer of the newest known snapshot and the
newest close, compared as instants (a journal day is a close only once its 16:00 ET has
passed), so it can be a close. 1m/3m/ytd/all end on `latest` when it is newer than their
last close; 1d/1w end on it only when `latest_at` falls inside the window. Points ascend in
time but not strictly: snapshot rows sharing a `captured_at` both appear.
`previous_close` is the close before the New York day `latest` belongs to; `change_today`
is None unless that day is today (weekends, before the day's first snapshot). A net
liquidation of 0 or less is unknown. Every figure is None when unknown - never 0.0.

AlternativeStrike.title: AlternativeStrike
AlternativeStrike.description: Another contract assessed on the same underlying during the same run.

ApprovalDetail.title: ApprovalDetail
ApprovalDetail.description: One approval in full, with the joined enrichment.

ApprovalRollFrom.title: ApprovalRollFrom
ApprovalRollFrom.description:
The short a roll buys back, from the frozen snapshot's ``roll_from`` (2026-10-11 roll
redesign). The mids are what the roll was priced at when it was proposed, per share: a quote,
never a fill.

ApprovalSummary.title: ApprovalSummary
ApprovalSummary.description: One row in the approvals list.

AssessedRunSummary.title: AssessedRunSummary
AssessedRunSummary.description: One past full-scan run, for browsing history in the Assessed tab.

Bar.title: Bar
Bar.description:
One daily OHLCV bar in lightweight-charts' expected field names.

``time`` is a ``YYYY-MM-DD`` string (lightweight-charts accepts the date prefix of an
ISO timestamp for a daily series). No client-side remapping is needed.

BarsResponse.title: BarsResponse
BarsResponse.description:
Daily bars with server-side SMA 50 and 200 overlays.

``sma50``/``sma200`` are parallel lists aligned to ``bars``: ``None`` until enough
data exists to compute the moving average at that index, then the value. Computed
server-side from ``daily_bars`` so the chart and the technical panel can never disagree.

BuyCandidateOut.title: BuyCandidateOut
BuyCandidateOut.description:
One buy-to-own recommendation, rendered exactly as the scan scored it.

The web layer does no re-scoring: every field below is the value
``generate_buy_candidates`` produced at scan time, persisted via
``BuyCandidateRow`` and read back unmodified so the site and Telegram can never
disagree about what the system thinks.

CallContextOut.title: CallContextOut
CallContextOut.description: One Claude call and the context blocks its prompt carries (static: ``claude_calls.CALLS``).

CampaignPnl.title: CampaignPnl
CampaignPnl.description: A wheel cycle: every option leg on a symbol, plus the stock leg.

ClaudeReviewPayload.title: ClaudeReviewPayload
ClaudeReviewPayload.description:
Claude's five review fields, surfaced separately — never one prose blob.

Telegram renders these as one chat bubble; the console renders them as five
labelled sections beside the numbers they refer to. ``rolling_considerations``
is the fifth and may be empty on the full-universe path.

CloseReason.title: CloseReason
CloseReason.description:
Why a short option was bought back — stamped on the closing order and its BUY fill.

`VerdictOutcome.CLOSED_EARLY` says only *that* a leg closed before expiry; this says why,
so profit-takes can be analysed apart from loss exits, rolls and hand-placed closes.

CommandKind.title: CommandKind
CommandKind.description: Every intent the web layer can enqueue. Later milestones register handlers.

CommandStatus.title: CommandStatus
CommandStatus.description:
The status of a command, returned by ``GET /commands/{id}`` and ``POST /commands``.

``confirm_token`` is present only while a live-mode order-reaching intent is
awaiting its second confirmation (§4.6). It is returned so the owner — the
only role that can reach these routes — can supply it back via
``POST /commands/{id}/confirm``; it is cleared the moment the command is
confirmed or expired, and is absent in paper mode entirely.

DayCalendarDay.title: DayCalendarDay
DayCalendarDay.description: One New York day's realised P&L: what closed that day, after commissions.

DayFact.title: DayFact
DayFact.description:
One line of a closed or rolled trade's reasoning. ``source`` is who said it: ``system``
lines are worked out from stored fills, alerts and the roll policy's own log; ``claude``
lines are Claude's stored view, which the web always labels as Claude's.

DayReview.title: DayReview
DayReview.description:
Claude's stored review of an opened trade, field for field the API's ClaudeReviewPayload
(src/api/models/options.py) so the web renders it with the proposal card's Why disclosure.

DayRolledTo.title: DayRolledTo
DayRolledTo.description: The leg a roll opened (the buy-back and the new short share one combo order).

DayTrade.title: DayTrade
DayTrade.description:
One executed trade on one New York day, as a Home card (web, 2026-10-15).

Money is USD for the whole position, never per share. ``premium``, ``bought_back`` and
``commissions`` are positive numbers; the card signs them. Unknown is None, never 0.0.
``net_pnl`` is the realised result after every commission, set only once the trade is
closed. ``capital`` is the cash held aside (a put), the shares' strike value (a call) or the
most a spread can lose.

DayTradesResponse.title: DayTradesResponse
DayTradesResponse.description: The trades opened, closed or rolled on one New York day (Home's "Done today").

DossierEvent.title: DossierEvent
DossierEvent.description:
An upcoming dated catalyst (not earnings) that the model proposed and Python verified.

``id`` is ``<SYM>:E<n>``; ``evidence`` is the ``C<id>`` of the news cluster that states the
date and ``quote`` the text of that cluster around it. Python keeps an event only when its
date is written in that cluster's text, so it is data, not prose.

DossierFact.title: DossierFact
DossierFact.description:
One deterministic line of a ticker dossier. ``id`` is ``<SYM>:F<n>`` so a reviewer can cite
it next to the candidate's own facts without a clash.

DossierOut.title: DossierOut
DossierOut.description: One name's notes: Python's numbers and health, Claude's story and profile, verified events.

DossierReported.title: DossierReported
DossierReported.description:
A figure quoted from the news about a name, kept apart from the story (OI-E10).

``text`` is a short statement of the figure (120 characters at most) and ``cluster_id`` the
``C<id>`` of the news cluster that states it. Python keeps an item only when every number in
``text`` is written in that cluster's text as the model was shown it, so the figure is the
news's, not the system's: every reader labels it "Reported in news (not computed by the
system)" and never mixes it into the story.

DroppedOut.title: DroppedOut
DroppedOut.description: A story the triage kept out of the picture, or one the market reaction promoted later.

EquityCurve.title: EquityCurve
EquityCurve.description:
Points, and the days between the first and last point that have no point.

`gaps` exists so the chart can render a gap rather than a straight line across a week
nobody measured.

FillSummary.title: FillSummary
FillSummary.description:
One fill against an order. Defined here (ahead of Task 2.3's orders/fills section)
because ``ApprovalDetail`` below references it for the approval-to-fill lineage.

The contract fields (web overhaul Part 3) come from the order's frozen snapshot, then its
candidate; each is ``None`` when neither is on record, never ``""`` or ``0``.

HeadlinesResponse.title: HeadlinesResponse
HeadlinesResponse.description: The newest headlines for one symbol, newest first (the position page's news section).

IdealZonePayload.title: IdealZonePayload
IdealZonePayload.description: The denormalised ideal zone from ``RiskVerdictRow`` (lo / hi / min_credit).

IncomeTarget.title: IncomeTarget
IncomeTarget.description:
The monthly income goal behind Home's pay card (web, 2026-10-15). Display only: nothing in
the trading path reads it.

``fixed``: ``amount`` dollars a month. ``pct_of_account``: ``pct`` percent of the account's
value at the month's start. ``pct_of_amount``: ``pct`` percent of ``base`` dollars the
operator names (a number that does not move with the account). ``off``: no target. Fields
that do not belong to the mode must be absent, so a stored row can never disagree with itself.

IncomeTargetResponse.title: IncomeTargetResponse
IncomeTargetResponse.description:
The monthly income target in force and where it came from (web setting, the legacy
`web.monthly_income_target_pct`, or none).

IndexRegime.title: IndexRegime
IndexRegime.description: One index's persisted regime: the daily base, today's intraday escalation, the result.

LedgerClose.title: LedgerClose
LedgerClose.description: One closing order's share of a trade (a trade may close in several orders).

LedgerFilters.title: LedgerFilters
LedgerFilters.description: Echoed back on every response so the client can prove what it is looking at.

LedgerTrade.title: LedgerTrade
LedgerTrade.description: One opening option order and everything that closed it (spec §4.2, R3, R4, R9, R10).

LeveragedLimitOut.title: LeveragedLimitOut
LeveragedLimitOut.description: A leveraged ETF's per-trade ceiling as a fraction of the regime's own (ruling 35).

LineItemValue.title: LineItemValue
LineItemValue.description: One normalised line item for one period, traceable to its filing.

MarketPicture.title: MarketPicture
MarketPicture.description:
The shared, persistent picture of the market every ``claude -p`` call reads.

Written only by the news process (``src/news/picture.py``); every number in it is computed by
Python, the story descriptions are the model's prose and are grounded before they are saved.
Enrichment: it reaches prompts and cards, never the engine, execution or sizing.

MarketRegime.title: MarketRegime
MarketRegime.description:
The market-wide state the sizing limits follow (not a per-ticker label: see `Regime`).

Ordered calm to severe: normal, cautious, stressed, crisis. Classified deterministically
by `src/analytics/regime.py`; turned into limits by `src/engine/regime_limits.py`.

MonthCalendar.title: MonthCalendar
MonthCalendar.description:
A month of daily realised P&L (web, 2026-10-15). Only days something closed appear; a
missing day is a day with no close, not a day known to be flat.

MonthPay.title: MonthPay
MonthPay.description:
One month's options income as a pay stub (web Home, DESIGN.md "October pay").

Months are New York calendar months. `premium_collected` counts credit on legs SOLD in the
month; `bought_back` counts debit on legs BOUGHT BACK in the month (an expired or assigned
leg closes on its expiry date). Commissions are charged by side, once each: the sell-side
commission (`PnlLeg.open_commissions`) in the month the leg was opened, the rest in the
month it closed; a leg with no known split charges all of them to the month it opened.
When `strategy` is "all" or "spread" the figures include the book's spread positions: entry
credit and entry commission in the month opened, the exit debit and exit commission in the
month the spread finally closed. `target_pct` echoes the setting; `target` and
`progress_pct` are None - never 0.0 - when there is no target percentage or no month-start
account value.

NewsItem.title: NewsItem
NewsItem.description:
One news headline with its per-item VADER sentiment.

``sentiment`` is the VADER compound polarity in -1.0..+1.0 (0.0 = neutral/unavailable).
The frontend renders it as a labelled chip (label + tint, never colour-only).

NoiseSummary.title: NoiseSummary
NoiseSummary.description: What the triage kept out of the picture in the last 7 days (shown, never overruled).

OptionsCoverage.title: OptionsCoverage
OptionsCoverage.description:
What the on-demand options lens could actually check.

``option_chain`` is always ``false`` in P1 — the API process holds no IBKR
connection, so ``atm_open_interest``/``atm_spread_pct`` stay ``UNKNOWN`` and the
response says so rather than the UI quietly showing blanks.

OptionsLensResponse.title: OptionsLensResponse
OptionsLensResponse.description:
``GET /research/{symbol}/options`` — the on-demand options-income checks lens.

``in_universe``/``tier`` reflect whether *symbol* is one of the ~46 `universe.yaml`
names (the "hot" tier, with full IV history) or anything else ("cold", best-effort).
``checks`` is the catalogue's `options` category only. `iv_rank`/`vrp_points` are read
real from the trading DB for a universe name; for an off-universe name with no
`iv_history` they resolve to `UNKNOWN` rather than a percentile invented from a short
series — `coverage.iv_history` names which case applied.

OrderSizingOut.title: OrderSizingOut
OrderSizingOut.description:
One sizing action linked to an order (``sizing_actions.order_id``): what the rules alone
would have sent, what was sent, and the reason as it was recorded (web overhaul Part 3).

PeriodStatement.title: PeriodStatement
PeriodStatement.description: Every line item for one reporting period.

PictureFact.title: PictureFact
PictureFact.description: One deterministic line of the market picture: a label and a value Python computed.

PictureRegime.title: PictureRegime
PictureRegime.description: One index's regime as the picture shows it (read from the trading process's record).

PictureStory.title: PictureStory
PictureStory.description:
A multi-week story the picture is tracking. Identity (id, title, start date) is kept by
Python; the description is the model's one-sentence tie to the numbered facts.

PnlBucket.title: PnlBucket
PnlBucket.description: Realised performance grouped by one key (a symbol, a strategy).

PnlLeg.title: PnlLeg
PnlLeg.description:
One option contract position, from the fill that opened it to whatever closed it.

`net_pnl` is None while the leg is open — never 0.0. An open leg has an unrealised
mark, not a realised result, and a zero in a realised column is a claim.

PositionDetailResponse.title: PositionDetailResponse
PositionDetailResponse.description:
One position as the page behind a Positions row shows it: where it stands now, and the
trade that opened it.

``kind`` follows the slug: ``option`` (``2026-11-21_P180``), ``shares`` or
``spread`` (``spread-<id>``). ``held`` is whether the latest snapshot still has it; a
contract that has since been closed, rolled or has expired is still answered from the system's
own fills, with ``closed`` saying how it ended. ``opened`` and ``closed`` are the same cards
Home's "Done today" shows (premium, commission, return, Claude's stored review, the reason),
so the figures on the two surfaces are one computation.

RealisedCalendarResponse.title: RealisedCalendarResponse
RealisedCalendarResponse.description: A month of daily realised P&L.

RecommendationsResponse.title: RecommendationsResponse
RecommendationsResponse.description:
``GET /research/recommendations`` — the buy list the scan produced.

``computed_at`` is the most recent full scan's compute time (the run the displayed
candidates came from). ``as_of`` is the request time. ``candidates`` is empty (not
an error) when no full scan has run yet; the route still returns 200 in that case.

RegimeChange.title: RegimeChange
RegimeChange.description: An effective-regime change, queued for a Telegram notice until ``sent``.

RegimeInputs.title: RegimeInputs
RegimeInputs.description:
Everything one index's regime was classified from (deterministic; see analytics/regime.py).

``vol`` is the VIX close for **both** indices (ruling 15), so the VIX thresholds mean the
same thing for SPY and QQQ. A field that could not be read, or that is a last close served
as live, is ``None`` and named in ``stale``: it is skipped by the classifier and never read
as calm.

RegimeLimitOut.title: RegimeLimitOut
RegimeLimitOut.description:
What one index's regime does to new cash-secured puts (``regime.csp`` in
``risk_limits.yaml``). Percentages are of the unscaled limit.

RegimeState.title: RegimeState
RegimeState.description: The persisted market regime for both indices (written only by the trading process).

ScoreBucket.title: ScoreBucket
ScoreBucket.description:
Realized performance of the closed trades whose signal value fell in one band.

Used by the score-vs-outcome report (N22) to check whether a higher `blended_score` — or a
higher per-component score — actually corresponds to better realized P&L / win rate. If it
doesn't, the scoring weights are not earning their keep and should be re-derived from this
evidence (human-edited config, per the fence).

ScoreOutcomeReport.title: ScoreOutcomeReport
ScoreOutcomeReport.description:
Score-vs-outcome evidence (N22): does the blended score / its components predict P&L?

Closed trades only (executed + settled). Read-only analysis that informs whether
`scoring_weights.yaml` should change — it never feeds the engine.

SeasonalityView.title: SeasonalityView
SeasonalityView.description: SPY's calendar-month tendency over the years the price provider covers (a weak signal).

SectorCard.title: SectorCard
SectorCard.description:
One sector's aggregate summary for the landing-page grid.

``avg_iv_rank`` is the differentiator: where premium is rich today, at a glance —
no consumer research site shows it. ``iv_rank_count`` is the number of members that
actually contributed to that average, so a one-name average is visible as such
(and ``avg_iv_rank`` is ``None`` when no member has IV history).
``change_pct`` is ``None`` (never ``0``) when no member has a priced quote.
Cards are ordered by ``avg_iv_rank`` descending on the client, since premium
richness is the reason to look.

SectorMover.title: SectorMover
SectorMover.description: One symbol and its daily change, for the best/worst corner of a sector card.

SentimentDetail.title: SentimentDetail
SentimentDetail.description:
Composite social + news sentiment for one symbol — enrichment only.

``overall`` (0-100, 50 = neutral, ``None`` = no data from any source) is the single
number that feeds scoring via :attr:`ScoreCard.sentiment_score`. The per-source fields,
counts, 1-day velocity, and headline are surfaced to Claude and the Telegram deep-dive
card to *explain* the read; they never reach the risk engine or position sizing.

SignalCorrelation.title: SignalCorrelation
SignalCorrelation.description:
How one signal relates to realized P&L over closed trades.

`pearson_r` is the linear correlation of the signal with realized P&L; the low/high split
contrasts mean P&L for the bottom vs top half of the signal's range — a coarse, robust
read that doesn't assume linearity.

SizingActionOut.title: SizingActionOut
SizingActionOut.description:
One row of the sizing record (``sizing_actions``): a cash-secured put the regime, the
scale-in ladder, the leveraged-ETF ceiling or Claude's cut trimmed or held back.

SizingGroupOut.title: SizingGroupOut
SizingGroupOut.description:
One line of the sizing record: a kind of action and what it withheld, as
``src/claude/eval/sizing_counterfactual.py::summarize`` reports it (key ``<kind>:<split>``,
or ``claude_overrides`` for Claude's cuts, whose ``kind`` is ``claude_cut``).

A positive P&L is what the withheld contracts would have **earned**: the action cost that
much (for ``regime_floor_lot`` the valued contracts are the lots the floor let through, so
positive means letting them through paid). Rows not yet valued count in ``count`` and not
in ``resolved``. A ``pushed_out`` line is counted and never valued, so its figures are None.

SizingRecordResponse.title: SizingRecordResponse
SizingRecordResponse.description: The sizing record, read by a human (the live-cutover gate's step 4). Display only.

Source.title: Source
Source.description: Where a number came from. A Black-Scholes delta must not look like an IBKR one.

SpreadMenuItemOut.title: SpreadMenuItemOut
SpreadMenuItemOut.description:
One lettered spread on a pick menu, flattened from the stored SpreadMenuItem. Credits are
per share; every figure was computed by src/spreads/menu.py when the menu was built.

SpreadPickOut.title: SpreadPickOut
SpreadPickOut.description: One menu Claude was shown, its choice, and what the service did with it.

SummaryOut.title: SummaryOut
SummaryOut.description:
The AI narrative over computed values. Enrichment — influences nothing.

Every number the model used was passed in via ``ResearchContext``; the model never
calculates. ``caveats`` always carries the quantitative limit. ``model`` and
``data_as_of`` make a stale summary visibly stale.

SystemPerformanceResponse.title: SystemPerformanceResponse
SystemPerformanceResponse.description: The score-vs-outcome report plus verdict agreement — P3-P4 M6's fenced read (Task 6.1).

UniverseResponse.title: UniverseResponse
UniverseResponse.description:
The parsed universe.yaml: four lists (each with override provenance for the
overridable two), the sector map, strike-band overrides. ``editable`` is ``true`` —
Task 7.4 is the write path this shape describes.

VerdictAgreement.title: VerdictAgreement
VerdictAgreement.description: How often Claude's verdict matched the deterministic baseline, and how each did.

Warning.title: Warning
Warning.description: One surfaced caveat. ``level`` drives the icon/tint; never colour-only.

WatchlistItem.title: WatchlistItem
WatchlistItem.description:
One row of the user's watchlist, with the fields the landing table needs.

``price`` ships as ``Sourced<float>`` so its provenance and staleness are explicit.
``checks`` is the aggregate {passed, evaluable, unknown} — the full per-check payload
lives on the ticker page (M5), one click away. ``iv_rank`` is read-only from the
trading DB's iv_history; ``None`` when the symbol has no IV history.

WatchlistResponse.title: WatchlistResponse
WatchlistResponse.description: ``GET /watchlist`` — the user's tracked symbols, scoped to their user_id.

src__api__models__research__SummaryRespo.title: SummaryResponse
src__api__models__research__SummaryRespo.description:
``GET/POST /research/{symbol}/summary``.

``state`` is ``ready`` (summary present), ``stale`` (cached but past TTL),
``unavailable`` (no summary; a GET made no model call), or ``pending`` (a POST
generation was attempted but failed soft). ``reason`` explains ``unavailable``/
``pending`` so the panel can show why and prompt a Generate/retry action.
